```{r setup, include=FALSE}

library(capnet)
library(dplyr)
repo_root <- normalizePath("../..")
source("helpers.R")
source("experiments.R")
source("simulation.R")
results_dir <- file.path(repo_root,"manuscript/results")
sim <- if (params$rerun) paper_simulation() else readRDS(file.path(results_dir,"simulation.rds"))
```

This is a **replacement experiment**, not a reconstruction of the undocumented
single dataset behind the earlier manuscript Tables 1 and 2. The design and grid
below are fixed before comparing performance. All replications, including those
where capping hurts, enter the summaries.

## Data-generating process

There are 10 independent replications, each with 400 training and 100 test
observations and eight predictors. Latent rows are multivariate Gaussian with
zero mean and covariance $\Sigma_{jk}=0.5^{|j-k|}$. The response is
$y_i=X_i^{*\top}\beta+\epsilon_i$, where
$\beta=(2.5,1.9,1.3,0.9,0.8,0,0,0)^\top$ and $\epsilon_i\sim N(0,1)$.
Observed predictors are $X=X^*+E$.

The **homoskedastic control** has independent $E_{ij}\sim N(0,0.25^2)$.
In the **mixture scenario**, predictors 1 and 2 instead have noise standard
deviation 10. The spike probability is 0.10 in training and 0.20 in the test
batch; otherwise their noise standard deviation is 0.25. All other
predictors retain standard deviation 0.25. Both scenarios share latent rows,
response noise, and base proxy-noise draws within each replication. Training
and test rows are independent; there is no response scaling on the test data.
The mixture setting is an explicit test-time stress shift from a 10% training
spike rate to a 20% test-batch rate.
Replication $r$ uses seed `20261112 + r`.

## Training-only calibration

Each replication/scenario selects `lambda.min` with ten-fold `cv.glmnet`,
`alpha = 0.5`, and training-column standardization. Folds use seed
`100000 + r`. That same lambda is held fixed across every cap configuration,
so the comparison changes contribution regularization rather than retuning the
coefficient penalty.

Let $b_j^{\rm uni}$ be the training univariate OLS slope. Define
$B_j=\max\{|b_j^{\rm uni}|q_{0.95}(|X_{\cdot j}|),0.05s_y\}$ and
$L_j=\kappa B_j$. The quantile, slopes, and response standard deviation use
training rows only. This puts the ceiling in contribution units; the floor
avoids nearly zero ceilings for weak training correlations.

We cross $\kappa\in\{0.5,1,2,4\}$ with
$\gamma\in\{0.1,1,10,100\}$. The uncapped baseline has $\gamma=0$ and
is fit once per replication/scenario. Test responses enter **only** the MSE.

Joint evaluation fits once using all 100 test covariate rows in the penalty;
this is a conditional/transductive comparison. Walk evaluation re-optimizes
on each test row (`walk = 1`) with the training data held fixed. Neither
scheme uses test responses in estimation. No test-grid winner is presented as
an independently selected deployment model.

sim$config

## Tables 1 and 2

Entries are mean test MSE across the 10 independent replications.

```{r mixture-tables}
for (evaluation in c("joint","walk")) {
  cat("\n", evaluation, " evaluation\n")
  print(knitr::kable(sim$summary |>
    filter(scenario=="mixture", .data$evaluation==.env$evaluation) |>
    select(gamma,kappa,mse,paired_delta), digits=4))
}
```

`paired_delta` is capped MSE minus the uncapped MSE from the **same** replication.
Its standard error uses those paired differences; negative values favor
capping. Report the full grid rather than interpreting its minimum as a tuned
model's validated performance.

## Homoskedastic control

```{r control}
knitr::kable(sim$summary |> filter(scenario=="homoskedastic") |>
  select(evaluation,gamma,kappa,mse,paired_delta),digits=4)
```

The control checks the cost of capping when large observed values are mostly
informative signal. A penalty that helps noisy proxies need not help here.

## Numerical checks and reproduction

```{r diagnostics}
stopifnot(nrow(sim$raw)==10*2*(2+2*4*4),all(is.finite(sim$raw$mse)))
sim$summary |> group_by(scenario,evaluation) |>
  summarise(reduced_rows=sum(reduced_rows), .groups="drop")
```

The runner rejects non-finite predictions and unsuccessful joint-fit stops.
Walk-forward fitting can retry with a lower gamma; reduced rows are counted
rather than silently treated as fits at the requested penalty.

From the repository root, run `bash tools/reproduce_paper.sh` to install the
current source into an isolated temporary R library, execute all experiments,
export tables/figures, and render these reports. Per-replication results and
paired summaries are in `manuscript/results/simulation-*.csv`; session metadata
and input/source checksums are saved alongside them. Runtime is not an outcome
of this simulation, and changing worker count does not change the specified RNG
streams.
